A_retraction_verbatim.retracted_claim: the played output was too quiet (-42..-47 dBFS) and the listener benefit is a measured negative
A_retraction_verbatim.why_invalid: the driver saves the LAST 16384 frames of the ring, i.e. 0.336 s. The alternating run was 2.4 s with a 2.0 s source, so the saved window starts at 2.064 s and ends at 2.400 s - entirely AFTER the source ended. The levels therefore describe the decay tail, not program material, and no loudness statement can be made from them.
A_retraction_verbatim.what_survives: the same-window arm difference (1.91 dB over the four arms, gate excluded; C independently got 1.905 dB) may be kept as a same-window comparison, but it is not a loudness measurement either.
A_retraction_verbatim.what_was_also_wrong: the earlier 1.38 dB summary included the gate run in the zero-arm mean; the four-arm mean is 1.91 dB.
A_retraction_verbatim.correct_method_for_a_real_measurement: the run duration must be no longer than the saved window (0.336 s) so that the capture falls inside the source, or the capture length must be made configurable. Neither was done here, and no new audible trial was spent.
A_retraction_verbatim.consequence_for_the_freeze: the audible-benefit question is OPEN again: it is neither a measured negative nor a measured positive. What stands is the 322 Hz three-point verdict (cancellation_holds) and every listener record as a record.
